candidates.draft_body:
Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) First Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan I) (c. 600 AD)

SALVATION-HISTORY RETELLING — the longest chapter in 1 Meqabyan (49 verses) and the most explicit retelling of the biblical narrative in the entire book. Compresses canonical and deuterocanonical history from CAIN THROUGH ESTHER into a single sweep. Function: provides the Meqabyan reader with the scriptural-context for the trilogy's martyrologies, locating Maqabis-of-Benjamin's witness within the longer arc of Israel's faithful + unfaithful exemplars. Parallels the Sirach 44-50 'Praise of Famous Men' genre, Hebrews 11 'faith heroes' chapter, 1 Maccabees 2:51-60 Mattathias's deathbed roll-call, and 4 Maccabees 18:11-13 + 18:7-8 (per CROSS_REFERENCE_APPENDIX-broadened 2 Mq parallels). The Meqabyan version's distinctive integration of Esther into the patriarchal-prophetic roll is a Tewahedo-canonical reception emphasis.

Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) First Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan I) (c. 600 AD)

ESTHER integration in the salvation-history catalog — the Cain-to-Esther sweep that the chapter compresses (per intro: 'compresses the canonical and deuterocanonical history from CAIN THROUGH ESTHER into a single sweep'). Esther's inclusion alongside the patriarchal-prophetic figures is DISTINCTIVE: the Tewahedo broader-canon includes Esther + Judith + Susanna + Tobit as exemplary-faithful-women alongside the Sirach 44-50 'Praise of Famous Men' male-roster. Meqabyan's Cain-to-Esther structure mirrors Sirach 44 (Praise of Famous Men) + Hebrews 11 (faith heroes) + 1 Maccabees 2:51-60 (Mattathias's deathbed roll-call) + 4 Maccabees 18:11-13 (mother's-virginity-speech with Adam-to-Daniel patriarchal-roll). Esther specifically appears as the queen-who-saved-her-people-through-courage-and-prayer (Esther 4:14-16 'who knoweth whether thou art come to the kingdom for such a time as this?'). Tewahedo Esther-tradition: Esther is one of the eight canonical female-exemplars in the Sǝnkǝsar.

Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) First Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan I) (c. 600 AD)

**ETHIOPIA NAMED — SECOND REFERENCE** in 1 Mq (paired with 25:9). The chapter's salvation-history sweep climaxes (vv. 35-49) with geographic-eschatological projection: Ethiopia + Saba + India + Nubia named together at the conclusion of the Cain-to-Esther historical-compression. The second-naming reinforces the first (25:9): Ethiopia is not merely a passing-geographic-reference but a STRUCTURAL-THEMATIC ANCHOR — the canonical Meqabyan text twice names Ethiopia within its homiletic-prophetic horizon. This dual-naming is the strongest INTERNAL-EVIDENCE for the text's ETHIOPIAN-SELF-RECEPTION as part of the Aksumite-and-Tewahedo biblical self-understanding. The Meqabyan-corpus is not merely a Tewahedo-canonical-text that happens to be preserved in Geʽez; it is a text that EXPLICITLY SITUATES ITSELF within the Ethiopian-Christian geographic-horizon. Tewahedo readers receive the verse as direct-prophetic-recognition of their tradition.
